newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's chief negotiator enters hostage compound.
newsitem.headline: Peru's chief negotiator enters hostage compound.

text.p: The Peruvian government's chief negotiator in the hostage crisis, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, on Saturday entered the Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels were holding 103 VIP hostages.

It was the first time during the hostage crisis -- now in its 11th day -- that a government official had entered the residence and apparently signalled the first direct contact between the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels and the administration of President Alberto Fujimori.

Palermo entered the fortified compound around 12:50 p.m. local time (1750 GMT) after a half-hour meeting with Michel Minnig of the Red Cross -- the official mediator in the crisis -- and Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, who both spent one hour and 40 minutes inside the residence earlier on Saturday.
Minnig and Cipriani accompanied the education minister inside the compound, where about 20 heavily-armed guerrillas have mined the grounds.

Fujimori has flatly rejected rebel demands for the release of their jailed MRTA comrades. The president, who has spoken in public only once during the siege, told the guerrillas a non-violent "way out" could be considered only after they released all their hostages and laid down their arms.

Since storming the residence on Dec. 17, the rebels have released about 400 hostages, but negotiations seemed to be deadlocked after they had freed only three more captives since a mass release on Sunday of 225 hostages.
The rebels have kept the hostages they consider most useful as bargaining chips, including top government officials, Japanese VIPs, some foreign diplomats and the president's brother Pedro Fujimori.
